clue.text: A light blow followed by a cry of pain

parts.note: to blow is what the wind does; wind as a gust or blast
ow is what someone yells when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone takes a gentle punch and then yelps in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like an adjective describing the blow, but it is a noun: a light is a pane that lets daylight in. 'followed by' simply puts the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture and glazing a light is any opening or pane admitting daylight, such as a glazed opening in a wall.

clue.text: Single boy or girl

parts.note: single means one, the Roman numeral I
Rene is a French boy's name

explanation.surface: A form asks whether a lone child is male or female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is only a link between wordplay and definition; the boy's name RENE follows I to make a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female given name, so it is an example of a woman's or daughter's name.

clue.text: He's laid down poor diets must be changed

indicators.note: the words poor diets have to be altered, signalling a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A man has decreed that inadequate eating plans need reforming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid down' suggests a rule being imposed, but here it means money put down in a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has placed money in a bank account has lodged it there, which is what a depositor does.

clue.text: An in-flight weakening

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other, the article going inside the word for flight

parts.note: a bird's wing is its means of flight, as in 'on the wing'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loses strength mid-air during a plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in-flight' reads as one airline adjective, but 'in' is the container signal and 'flight' gives WING, which is split as W...ING around AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Waning describes something diminishing, like the moon after full, so it is losing strength.

clue.text: Wildlife sanctuary for saving threatened species

definitions.text: Wildlife sanctuary for saving threatened species

parts.words: Wildlife sanctuary for saving threatened species
parts.note: reads like a modern conservation reserve, but describes the Biblical vessel that carried pairs of every animal through the Flood

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch built a great boat to preserve every kind of animal from the Flood, a floating refuge for endangered creatures.

clue.text: "A woman sat in unwomanly rags, plying her ______." (Hood)

definitions.text: "A woman sat in unwomanly rags, plying her ______." (Hood)

parts.words: "A woman sat in unwomanly rags, plying her ______." (Hood)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Thomas Hood's poem The Song of the Shirt, about an exploited seamstress at work

explanation.walkthrough: The missing words complete a line of Thomas Hood's 1843 poem The Song of the Shirt, about a poor seamstress sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress plies sewing tools, the pointed implement and its yarn, which Hood's poem names to complete the line.

clue.text: Behind everyone else, in spite of everything

explanation.definitionFit: Literally coming later than the rest; idiomatically, nevertheless or despite all that happened.

clue.text: A fool accepts credit — though not much

indicators.note: the fool takes in the credit, so its letters go inside

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A gullible person is given some credit, though only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'credit' sounds like praise but is the bookkeeping abbreviation CR, which goes inside SAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a tiny piece or fragment, so only a small amount.

clue.text: Having a stretch in the long grass may be recalled

indicators.note: in says the stretch sits within the long grass

parts.note: reeds are tall grasses growing in wet places
a tract is a stretch of land

explanation.surface: Something lying out in tall grass might be remembered later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch' suggests lying down for a rest, but it is a tract of land, placed inside REED.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to withdraw a statement, just as a product or remark is called back.

clue.text: Person in a bad way with depression making answer

indicators.note: something in a bad way is in poor shape, so the letters of person are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder for the rearrangement
a dent is a hollow or depression in a surface

explanation.surface: Someone who is struggling with low mood gives a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood but is a physical dent. 'in a bad way' rearranges PERSON into RESPON.
explanation.definitionFit: Respondent as an adjective means replying, giving a reply to a question or a legal petition.

clue.text: Soldiers going around at 22dn

indicators.note: the soldiers encircle the word at, a container signal

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Troops are circling at a certain pace.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the answer at 22 down, SPEED: a rate is a speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rate means velocity or pace, the cross-referenced word.

clue.text: A boy has to stop outside at a certain time

indicators.note: the stopping word goes round the others, so it is outside them

parts.note: to seal a gap is to stop it up
taken as written
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A lad must stand outside waiting until a fixed hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' is a link; SEAL is split as SE...AL around A SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal things occur only during particular periods of the year.

clue.text: Check about a remission

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, with the checking word going around the a

parts.note: to repel an attack is to check it

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to examine a reduction in a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals that REPEL goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission can mean cancelling a debt or penalty, which is what revoking a law does.

clue.text: Notice a blemish

explanation.definitionFit: To see or catch sight of something; also a mark or pimple on the skin.

clue.text: He makes too much from the tipster here, says the Cockney

indicators.note: a Londoner of that kind drops initial aitches, so the words are spoken with here as 'ere

parts.note: a prophet is someone giving tips on the future, and here is pronounced without its h

explanation.surface: A man earns excessively by following the racing tipster on hand, according to a Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their h's, so 'prophet 'ere' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A profiteer is someone who exploits shortages for excessive gain.

clue.text: Ill-health as a consequence of salt-mine ill-treatment

definitions.note: singular noun phrase standing for a plural list of sicknesses

indicators.note: rough handling of the words salt-mine signals that their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Miners fall sick after harsh conditions underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical disorders or sicknesses together amount to poor health.

clue.text: Leaderless men bolt without a shot

indicators.note: the word men loses its leading letter
without in the old sense of outside, the bolting word surrounding a

parts.note: to bolt food is to devour it

explanation.surface: Men without a leader run away without firing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so DEVOUR wraps A; 'bolt' is gulping, not fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a shot at something is to make an attempt or effort.

clue.text: High-level illumination for the supporter?

parts.note: a window set above a door lighting a hallway, jokingly read as a lamp belonging to a sports enthusiast

explanation.definitionFit: A semicircular window above a door lets light into a hall from high up.

clue.text: Tie up and go ashore, though it's a wild area

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up
to land is to disembark from a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor secures the boat and steps ashore, though it is rough country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'though it's' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorland is open uncultivated upland, rough heath country.

clue.text: The old monarch cheated none

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating them
O is zero, i.e. none

explanation.surface: A former king deceived nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido was the legendary queen of Carthage in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the legendary founder-queen of Carthage, an ancient ruler.

clue.text: One of the eccentric Breton sisterhood

definitions.text: One of the eccentric Breton sisterhood

indicators.note: odd or off-centre, signalling that the letters of Breton are jumbled

explanation.surface: One nun from an odd order in Brittany.
explanation.walkthrough: The sisterhood is the three Bronte novelists, Charlotte, Emily and Anne; 'eccentric' rearranges BRETON.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, Emily and Anne were the famous literary siblings of Haworth.

clue.text: Book for a young lady .-.a pound

parts.note: miss is a title for a young unmarried woman
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A book bought for a girl cost one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the liturgical volume containing the texts of the Mass.

clue.text: Children change inside for race

indicators.note: inside places the change within the word for children

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants
P (penny) is small change

explanation.surface: Children swap places indoors before a running contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like a verb but is a coin, P for penny, put inside SEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to move fast, to hurry along.

clue.text: Rosemary, Basil and the others are collected here for a simple song

definitions.text: Rosemary, Basil and the others are collected here

parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal plant
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: People named Rosemary and Basil gather to perform an easy tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosemary and Basil look like people but are plants, collected in herb gardens or dried-plant archives; 'simple' is the noun for a medicinal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbaria are collections of dried plant specimens, plural of herbarium.

clue.text: Private hotel Her Majesty used

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel or pub with rooms
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The Queen stayed at an exclusive guesthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private and not shown to others.

clue.text: Only requiring a couple of notes

parts.note: me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tune needing just two notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, as in a mere child.

clue.text: Fresh weight given to EEC agriculture by Britain

definitions.text: Fresh weight given to EEC agriculture by Britain

parts.note: green means fresh, new or unripe
a pound is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Britain lends new clout to European farming.
explanation.walkthrough: This was the special exchange rate for sterling used in the EEC's Common Agricultural Policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's agricultural exchange rate under the European Community farm policy was a special notional currency value.

clue.text: Misdirected, so it's believed

indicators.note: the prefix mis- means wrongly, so the rest of the word is badly arranged

explanation.surface: Something sent astray is thereby trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word splits: 'Mis' is the anagram signal and 'directed' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to accept it as true.

clue.text: Blunders made in terror-some really bad.

indicators.note: in shows the letters lie within the run of words terror some

explanation.surface: Mistakes made in a panic, some very serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors are mistakes, slips or gaffes.
